answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because fable only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. In practice glacier is enforced by the ledger itself: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any vine approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
